requirements.text: For the service that Priya currently owns, create a new service offering named Web Portal Register ... have me as its owner and it covers registering new users in the customer web portal ... business operational service that is used directly in production ... moderately critical
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_offering WHERE service_offering_id = 'SVCOFF_005' AND name = 'Web Portal Register' AND LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%register%' AND LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%customer%' AND LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%web%' AND LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%portal%' AND owned_by = 'USER_001' AND business_service = 'SVC_002' AND used_for = 'production' AND status = 'operational' AND service_classification = 'business' AND business_criticality = 'somewhat-critical'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (SVCOFF_005 after SVCOFF_004); the only offering the task creates
Priya is USER_002 Priya Sharma, the only user with that first name; the only service she owns is SVC_002 Customer Portal
'me' is the acting user USER_001 Marcus Thompson
'business operational service ... used directly in production' read as service_classification = business, status = operational, used_for = production, as the benchmark check does
'moderately critical' read as business_criticality = somewhat-critical, the benchmark check's value, between the seed's critical and less-critical

short_description tested by the keywords register, customer, web, portal from 'registering new users in the customer web portal', as the benchmark check does; the request fixes the wording only loosely
org_id and the long description column are not tested: neither the request nor the benchmark check fixes them

requirements.text: update this incident to use the new service offering instead of its previous service offering
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_015' AND service_offering = 'SVCOFF_005'
assumptions: the incident assigned to Service Desk Operations (GROUP_002) that concerns an application crash is INC_015 'Application crash on startup'; no other GROUP_002 incident mentions a crash, and INC_012 'Critical application crash' is in GROUP_004
SVCOFF_005 is the id of the offering created above (next in sequence); its previous offering is SVCOFF_002 Web Portal Login
the service column (SVC_002) is not asked to change: the new offering belongs to the same service

requirements.text: change the incident description so that it clearly states what the new service offering is about ... the error actually occurs when navigating specifically to the new user registration screen
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_015' AND LOWER(description) LIKE '%crash%' AND LOWER(description) LIKE '%user%' AND LOWER(description) LIKE '%regist%' AND LOWER(description) LIKE '%customer%' AND LOWER(description) LIKE '%web%' AND LOWER(description) LIKE '%screen%' AND LOWER(description) LIKE '%portal%'
assumptions: the request fixes no wording; keywords kept from the benchmark check (crash and screen from the reporter's clarification, the rest from what the new offering covers)
the seed description ('Customer portal application crashes immediately after launch') lacks regist, user, web and screen, so the change is measurable
split from the same benchmark check as the service_offering change so each part can fail on its own

requirements.text: Send a report to the user who is currently assigned to resolve this incident with the subject Updated Service Offering and Deadline for Your Web Portal Registration Incident ... greet this assignee by their full name ... the incident (using its ID) has just been updated ... naming both the previous service offering and the new one ... highlight the new description ... fully resolved no later than the end of the current sprint, which finishes on Friday of this week

cells.subject: Updated Service Offering and Deadline for Your Web Portal Registration Incident

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_008' AND incident_id = 'INC_015' AND email = 'aisha.williams@techcorp.com' AND type = 'report' AND subject = 'Updated Service Offering and Deadline for Your Web Portal Registration Incident' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%aisha williams%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%inc_015%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%incident%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%updated%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%web portal login%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%web portal register%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%crash%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%user%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%regist%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%customer%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%web%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%screen%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%portal%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%scope%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%expectat%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%fully resolved%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%current%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%sprint%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%friday%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%week%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (NOTIF_008 after NOTIF_007); the only notification the task creates
the assignee of INC_015 is USER_004 Aisha Williams, aisha.williams@techcorp.com (seed); the notification table keys recipients by email
'send a report' read as type = report, as the benchmark check does
'using its ID' read as the incident_id INC_015, as in the benchmark check, not the number INC0000010
previous offering named as 'Web Portal Login' (SVCOFF_002 on the seed), new one as 'Web Portal Register'; both names must appear

the new description is tested in the message by the same keywords as the incident description requirement; '%scope%' kept from the benchmark check (the request says 'so they understand the real scope of the problem', not fixed as message wording)
deadline words (expectat, fully resolved, current, sprint, friday, week) taken from the request's own phrasing, as the benchmark check does
status not tested: neither the request nor the benchmark check fixes it

requirements.text: Locate the incident that is currently assigned to the Service Desk Operations group and that concerns an application crash (boundary: the other crash incident keeps its offering and description)

cells.description: Production application repeatedly crashing with memory errors

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_012' AND service_offering = 'SVCOFF_004' AND description = 'Production application repeatedly crashing with memory errors'
assumptions: selector boundary: INC_012 'Critical application crash' is the other crash incident on the seed but is assigned to GROUP_004 Infrastructure Team, not Service Desk Operations, so it must keep its offering and description
disagreement: A has this stay, B does not; kept because it is the boundary of the incident selector (the row a loose reading of 'concerns an application crash' would sweep in)

requirements.text: Locate the incident that is currently assigned to the Service Desk Operations group and that concerns an application crash (boundary: no other incident moves to the new offering)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE service_offering = 'SVCOFF_005' AND incident_id <> 'INC_015'
assumptions: boundary of the selector: the other five GROUP_002 incidents and INC_012 'Critical application crash' (GROUP_004) must not be re-pointed at the new offering
disagreement: B has this stay, A does not; kept because it is the other side of the selector's boundary (only the one located incident may move to SVCOFF_005)

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on the three benchmark checks (all kept), the new offering (SVCOFF_005, somewhat-critical, business, operational, production, owned by USER_001 under SVC_002), the two changes to INC_015 (offering SVCOFF_005; description keywords) and the report to Aisha Williams (NOTIF_008, tied to INC_015). The benchmark's incident check is carried by two requirements so each part can fail on its own. Created rows are anchored by the next id in sequence, which the benchmark's own checks do not test. The acting user is an admin, so the policy's role table permits every step.
disagreement: stay that INC_012 keeps its offering SVCOFF_004 and its description: A has it, B does not; kept as the boundary of the incident selector, INC_012 being the other crash incident on the seed but assigned to GROUP_004, not Service Desk Operations (logged on the requirement).
disagreement: stay that no incident other than INC_015 is on the new offering SVCOFF_005 (expected 0): B has it, A does not; kept as the other side of the selector's boundary, the other five GROUP_002 incidents and INC_012 must not be re-pointed (logged on the requirement).
disagreement: form of the LIKE predicates in cells: A prefixes each with LOWER(column), B writes the bare predicate on the column; kept B's, the convention of every other check file, the SQL being identical in both passes.
